2.2.a.title: Unsourced or unverified claims
2.2.a.original_text: Every reasonable attempt should be made by editors and individual journalists to verify the accuracy of reports prior to publication. Where such verification is not practicable, that fact shall be stated in the report.
2.2.a.obligation: Verify reports before publication. If verification is not practicable, say so in the report.
violation_conditions: the article makes significant factual claims or allegations
no source or verification is given for them
the article does not state that verification was not practicable
evidence_cues: claims without 'according to', 'police said', named sources
'it is reported that' with no source

2.2.b.title: Non-credible source
2.2.b.original_text: Every reasonable attempt should be made by editors and individual journalists to verify the accuracy of reports prior to publication.
2.2.b.obligation: Sources relied on should be credible (e.g. an expert or authority on the subject).
violation_conditions: a claim relies on a source
the source, as described in the article, has no apparent credibility or expertise on the subject
evidence_cues: social media posts as sole source

2.2.c.title: Irrelevant source
2.2.c.original_text: Every reasonable attempt should be made by editors and individual journalists to verify the accuracy of reports prior to publication.
2.2.c.obligation: Sources should be relevant to the incident being reported.
violation_conditions: a claim relies on a source
the source, as described in the article, has no connection to or knowledge of the incident
evidence_cues: quotes from people with no link to the event

2.5.title: Mixing comment, conjecture and fact
2.5.original_text: The press must distinguish clearly between comment, conjecture and fact.
2.5.obligation: Clearly distinguish comment, conjecture and fact.
violation_conditions: the article contains opinion or speculation
it is presented as established fact or not clearly marked as opinion

6.1.a.title: Insensitive or sensational treatment of shocking issues
6.1.a.original_text: In dealing with social issues of a particularly shocking or emotionally painful nature - such as atrocity, violence, drug abuse, brutality, sadism, sexual salacity and obscenity - the press should take special care to present facts, opinions, photographs and graphics with due sensitivity and discretion, subject to its duty to publish in the public interest.
6.1.a.obligation: Present shocking or painful issues with sensitivity and discretion.
violation_conditions: the article covers a shocking or emotionally painful issue
facts or opinions are presented sensationally, graphically or without discretion
the level of detail is not justified by the public interest

6.1.b.title: Excessive detail of method of murder
6.1.b.original_text: In dealing with social issues of a particularly shocking or emotionally painful nature - such as atrocity, violence, drug abuse, brutality, sadism, sexual salacity and obscenity - the press should take special care to present facts, opinions, photographs and graphics with due sensitivity and discretion, subject to its duty to publish in the public interest.
6.1.b.obligation: Do not report excessive detail of how a murder was committed.
violation_conditions: the article reports a murder
it gives excessive detail of the method (weapons, step-by-step actions, injuries)
evidence_cues: number and location of stab wounds

6.1.c.title: Excessive detail of method of criminal conduct
6.1.c.original_text: In dealing with social issues of a particularly shocking or emotionally painful nature - such as atrocity, violence, drug abuse, brutality, sadism, sexual salacity and obscenity - the press should take special care to present facts, opinions, photographs and graphics with due sensitivity and discretion, subject to its duty to publish in the public interest.
6.1.c.obligation: Do not report excessive detail of how a crime was committed (a how-to).
violation_conditions: the article reports a crime
it gives enough method detail that it could serve as instructions or glamorise the crime

6.2.i.title: Naming victims of sex crimes
6.2.i.original_text: In reporting accounts of crime or criminal case, publications shall not, unless it is both legally permitted and in the public interest - i. Name victims of sex crimes.
6.2.i.obligation: Do not name (or otherwise identify) victims of sex crimes.
violation_conditions: the article reports a sex crime
the victim is named or identifiable (name, photo, address, school, relationship to named person)
it is not both legally permitted and in the public interest
evidence_cues: naming a relative that identifies the victim
6.2.i.notes: Both exceptions must hold together (legally permitted AND public interest).

6.2.ii.title: Naming young accused persons
6.2.ii.original_text: In reporting accounts of crime or criminal case, publications shall not, unless it is both legally permitted and in the public interest - ii. Knowingly name any young person accused of a criminal offence who is below the age of 16 and who has no previous convictions.
6.2.ii.obligation: Do not knowingly name an accused person under 16 with no previous convictions.
violation_conditions: the person is accused of a criminal offence
the person is below 16
the person is named or identifiable
the article gives no indication of previous convictions
evidence_cues: school or address of a juvenile suspect
6.2.ii.notes: Covers accused persons only. Identifying child victims falls under 7.4.

6.2.iii.title: Identifying relatives of accused or convicted persons
6.2.iii.original_text: In reporting accounts of crime or criminal case, publications shall not, unless it is both legally permitted and in the public interest - iii. Identify without consent relatives of a person accused or convicted of a crime.
6.2.iii.obligation: Do not identify relatives of an accused or convicted person without their consent.
applies_to: family members of suspects or convicts
violation_conditions: the article reports on a person accused or convicted of a crime
a relative of that person is identified
there is no indication of the relative's consent

6.3.title: Promoting communal or religious discord
6.3.original_text: A journalist shall not knowingly or wilfully promote communal or religious discord or violence.
6.3.obligation: Do not knowingly promote communal or religious discord or violence.
violation_conditions: the article concerns ethnic, communal or religious groups
it frames content in a way that incites or promotes discord or violence between them
evidence_cues: calls to action against a group

6.4.i.title: Prejudicial or pejorative references
6.4.i.original_text: The press must avoid prejudicial or pejorative reference to a person's race, colour, religion, sex or to any physical or mental illness or disability.
6.4.i.obligation: Avoid prejudicial or pejorative references to race, colour, religion, sex, illness or disability.
violation_conditions: the article refers to one of these characteristics
the reference is prejudicial or pejorative
evidence_cues: derogatory terms for mental illness or disability

6.4.ii.title: Irrelevant identity details
6.4.ii.original_text: It must avoid publishing details of a person's race, caste, religion, sexual orientation, physical or mental illness or disability unless these are directly relevant to the story.
6.4.ii.obligation: Do not mention race, caste, religion, sexual orientation, illness or disability unless directly relevant.
violation_conditions: the article mentions one of these characteristics of a person
the characteristic is not directly relevant to the story
evidence_cues: 'a Muslim man', 'a Tamil youth' in crime stories where it's irrelevant
mentioning mental illness of a suspect without relevance

6.5.title: Excessive detail of suicide method
6.5.original_text: When reporting suicide, care should be taken not to give excessive detail of the method used.
6.5.obligation: Do not give excessive detail of the method used in a suicide.
violation_conditions: the article reports a suicide or attempted suicide
it gives excessive detail of the method (substance, dose, location, means, step-by-step)
evidence_cues: named poison or drug and amount
description of how/where the act was done

7.1.title: Intrusion into private and family life
7.1.original_text: The press shall exercise particular care to respect the private and family lives of individuals, their home, health and correspondence, including digital communications. Intrusions on this right to privacy without consent could be justified only by some over-riding public interest.
7.1.obligation: Respect private and family life, home, health and correspondence (including digital communications).
violation_conditions: private information is disclosed (family life, home, health, correspondence)
the individual is identifiable
there is no indication of consent
there is no overriding public-interest justification
evidence_cues: medical diagnosis of a named person

7.4.title: Intrusion into children's private lives
7.4.original_text: Young people should be free to complete their school years without unnecessary intrusion. Publication of material concerning a child's private life would be acceptable only if there was some exceptional public interest other than the fame, notoriety or position of his or her family or guardian.
7.4.obligation: Do not publish material about a child's private life without exceptional public interest.
violation_conditions: the article concerns a child's private life
the child is identifiable
there is no exceptional public interest (the family's fame does not count)
evidence_cues: details of a child's family problems
7.4.notes: Public interest here must be exceptional, a higher bar than other rules.

7.5.title: Intrusion into people in hospitals or institutions
7.5.original_text: The restrictions on intruding into privacy are particularly relevant to inquiries about individuals in hospitals or similar institutions, unless it serves the public interest.
7.5.obligation: Take particular care with privacy of people in hospitals or similar institutions.
applies_to: people in care homes, rehab, prisons or similar institutions
violation_conditions: the article concerns an identifiable person in a hospital or similar institution
it discloses private details about them
there is no public-interest justification
